check: Is the scene free of sustained periodic oscillation (bobbing, swaying, pulsing) of elements, other than an oscillation that is itself the mechanism being taught?
instruction: Do not make elements oscillate continuously; if the mechanism itself oscillates, show it for a bounded time.
threshold: no sustained periodic motion, especially near 0.2 Hz

check: Does the same kind of mechanism change (add, remove, move, update a value) use the same transition every time it occurs, and do different kinds of change use visibly different transitions?
instruction: Give each kind of change one transition and use it every time; make different kinds of change look different.

check: Does each quantitative axis keep one scale across states, and where rescaling is unavoidable, is the rescale shown as its own step before values change?
instruction: Keep axis scales fixed across states; if a rescale is unavoidable, animate it as a separate step before the values move.

check: Do appearing or transitioning elements leave visible text in place instead of pushing or reflowing text the learner may still be reading?
instruction: Reserve space for elements that appear later so visible text never moves.

check: Does a pause stay in effect until the learner resumes, rather than lasting only while a control is hovered or focused?
instruction: Make pause a toggle that holds until the learner resumes.
applies_when: scenes with automatic motion and a pause control

check: Do multi-line texts break at phrase or clause boundaries and never inside a word?
instruction: Break lines at punctuation or between phrases, never inside a word.

check: Is each sentence shown whole within one beat or step, not split across beats?
instruction: Keep each sentence within one beat; split long explanations into complete sentences or clauses.
applies_when: scenes whose text changes by beat or step

check: Are titles, annotations and data labels set horizontally (axis and line labels may deviate)?
instruction: Set titles, annotations and data labels horizontally; rotate only axis or line labels if needed.

check: Is all on-screen text free of grammatical errors, typos and awkward phrasing?
instruction: Write on-screen text with correct grammar and spelling and natural phrasing.

check: Are displayed numbers shown at the precision the learning target needs, without unneeded decimal places or digits?
instruction: Round displayed numbers to the precision the point needs.

check: Does the diagram form fit the relation it shows (change over time, comparison, part-whole, structure, flow)?
instruction: Choose the diagram form from the relation the scene must show.

check: Are parallel items (bars, nodes, list entries, states) arranged in an order that helps the learner interpret them (size, time, sequence, grouping)?
instruction: Order parallel items by a meaningful key such as size, time, sequence or group.

check: Does each chart use one horizontal and one vertical value axis, with no secondary value axis?
instruction: Do not add a second value axis; use two charts side by side instead.

check: Are the differences the learner must tell apart shown as clearly perceptible categorical differences rather than fine differences of angle, length or size?
instruction: Encode distinctions the learner must make with clearly different shapes, colors or positions, not fine differences of angle or length.

check: Are diagram elements simple schematic shapes that still make clear which entity each represents (by label or distinctive form)?
instruction: Draw entities as simple schematic shapes and make each one identifiable by a label or a distinctive form.

check: Does the diagram use the representations and notation of the domain that the intended learner will meet elsewhere, rather than idiosyncratic ones?
instruction: Use the domain's standard notation and diagram conventions.

check: Does the scene state on screen, as a short question or sentence, what the learner should understand from this card?
instruction: State on screen, in one short question or sentence, what this card is for.

check: Does the scene avoid questions or required interactions that only delay information the learner needs?
instruction: Ask the learner to act only where the action serves learning; do not gate needed information behind extra steps.

check: Does the scene show where the current step or phase sits in the whole sequence?
instruction: Show the current step or phase within the whole sequence (e.g. a step indicator or highlighted stage).
